item: A Stop through a loopback HTTP proxy is read as the Stop, a URL's credentials stay out of the failure sentence, and the inert DOTALL goes (R620)
summary: R620, three items in one PR. (a) A Stop through a LOOPBACK HTTP proxy (Privoxy chained to Tor) to an https target: the socket guard refuses the real destination in _guarded_tunnel, which urllib3 calls after _new_conn returned, so the fetcher wrote "request error for <url>: ('Connection aborted.', AirplaneModeError(\"airplane mode is engaged: refusing a network connection to '<host>'. ...\"))" (measured through the real guard, a loopback proxy, requests 2.34, urllib3 2.7.0 and 2.8.0; single quotes when the host holds one; the proxy receives no CONNECT byte). Before, no alternative of fetch_verdict._OFFLINE_RE read it and it was classified connect, a false 'not offline' that only the R320 switch read caught while the switch was still engaged; now a fourth alternative spells urllib3's construction from its first word with no gap. A host cannot write it: urllib3 writes 'Connection aborted.' once (connectionpool.py, for an OSError or an HTTPException; requests never), the tuple's second item is that exception's repr, and every such class on the fetch path opens its repr with its own name (BaseException's repr, or one of four overrides that do the same), so a host's words sit inside the quotes after a class name it cannot choose (BadStatusLine for a status line, OSError under ProxyError for a proxy's refused CONNECT); one class is named AirplaneModeError and its one writer opens with the guard's words. This narrows R320 for that one shape (it reads the whole construction, it does not widen), and the switch read stays for every other shape: the tests that pinned the shape as a non-match now pin it as a match, and the switch-clear direction uses a host's reset in the same wrapping. (b) failure_url wrote a URL's userinfo into the failure sentence (https://alice:hunter2@host/x, stored, served and shown); now the authority's userinfo and its @ are written ***@ (fixed length, the user name too, no whitespace and none of :/?#[]@, so host/port/path parse the same and the token stays one \S+), the span read wider than urlsplit and urllib3 (dropped tab/CR/LF skipped, leading whitespace skipped, any scheme before the first colon, authority to the first / ? # with the backslash, the last @), an @ in a path, query or fragment untouched, whitespace still percent-encoded, and it never raises (an unreadable input is written <url-withheld>). No consumer of 'request error for' parses the URL back out. The mask then covers every other sentence the fetcher writes with a caller's URL in it, so a credentialed URL that gets a 401 no longer lands raw in 'HTTP 401 for <url>': unsupported or malformed URL, HTTP <status> for, non-HTML content for, redirect to unsupported URL (the Location's URL, which a host chooses), too many redirects for, declared length ... exceeds, response exceeds (streamed and held), body read exceeded, robots.txt disallows, robots.txt for <scheme://netloc> could not be determined, and two log lines (the fetcher's unreadable proxy environment, the archive backfill's failed URL); the repr forms keep the repr around the masked URL. An ordinary URL is written exactly as before. Every reader was checked and reads the masked sentence as it read the raw one: fetch_verdict.classify_fetch_failure (the HTTP (\d{3}) search and its phrases), the pipeline's _failure_reason, the markets classify_fetch_failure and classify_failed_check (weather), the law board's _verdict_of, the anchored refusal read in the preflights, api/monitoring, events/feeds and law/track; none parses the URL back out, and no UI script parses these sentences. No existing test pinned one of them with a credentialed or whitespace URL through the fetcher, so none was changed. (c) The inert re.DOTALL is dropped (no '.' stood outside a class or an escape); the flags pin says re.IGNORECASE. (d) By TYPE, after Steward 3's security note (classified by type and never by words): before the fetcher writes 'request error for' (its one writer, EthicalFetcher._fetch_locked) it walks the live requests exception for an AirplaneModeError instance (__cause__, the exceptions in args, urllib3's MaxRetryError.reason; at most 8 deep and 64 nodes, a seen set, never through text; NOT __context__, which is whatever the caller's thread was handling when the request raised: followed, it made a fetch inside the except of a Stopped fetch, or of a bare guard refusal, read its own host's failure with the switch clear as the switch's, unretried and offline, the independent read's S1, reproduced with the real fetcher and a closed loopback port; every real shape is reached without it) and, if one is there, raises FetchFailed(KILL_SWITCH_REFUSAL) at once: no retry, no back-off, no host's text. Every reader reads that whole sentence as the switch's (_OFFLINE_RE's first alternative, the pipeline's _failure_reason, R614's refused_by_name and law/track's head read). It covers the direct shape (R616), the CONNECT shape (a) and one no words read: once R619 (PR #1855) guards putrequest, a plain http:// request line to a loopback proxy is refused before the proxy is reached and urllib3 writes it as ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', AirplaneModeError(...)) inside MaxRetryError, with no NewConnectionError and no 'Connection aborted.', so it read as connect (measured at #1855's head b4d743668 in a scratch worktree since removed; the live test drives R619's own putrequest guard, found among airplane._patch_points(), and skips on a branch without it, this one until #1855 lands; with this branch laid over that head it runs and passes, and fails with the args link dropped). Why no host can produce the type: the class has one constructor, airplane._guard (on this branch and at #1855's head, where R619's putrequest guard calls _guard and adds none), which raises only while the switch is engaged, the airplane half armed, the host not local and no egress window open, from a lookup, a connect, a CONNECT or a request line before any byte reaches the destination; a host's bytes become the libraries' own classes. Alternative 4 (and R616's alternative 2) stays as the net under the typed read: no live path needs it (the typed read runs first at its one writer) and no stored record does (every caller classifies a live exception's text, none re-reads a stored one); it is kept because R616 and R620(a) rule it, and because a link the bounded walk missed would still leave the real instance's repr, which a host cannot write. Over SOCKS, urllib3.contrib.socks raises NewConnectionError from the guard's error, so the walk finds it there too; that path is not exercised (PySocks is not installed). The cannot-resolve-host sentence (alternative 3) is written outside the requests handler and is still read by words. (e) The folds of the two security reads. An exception's own words after the URL lose its userinfo too (Steward 3 #1): requests quotes a URL it cannot prepare ('Failed to parse: https://u:pw@...'), so fetch_verdict.userinfo_secrets hands record_text and log_failure the whole userinfo and the user and the password apart (each also without the characters urllib.parse drops) at the request-error sentence, the proxy-environment log, the archive backfill log and the two persistence logs; a part under the scrub's four-character floor withholds the error's words whole instead. The live fetcher refuses such a URL before any request (_refuse_parser_mismatch), so this is the net under that refusal; a redirect hop's own userinfo is not among the secrets, stated (a hop with no http(s) scheme, no host or an authority urllib3 cannot parse is refused before it is requested). The robots-cache and host-schedule DEBUG lines write their key masked (failure_url, and failure_netloc for a bare netloc; Steward 3 #2). Stated, no code change: the wider mask can take the host urllib3 reads when the authority holds a backslash (https://u:p@evil.example\@good.example/x is written https://***@good.example/x), the safe choice for the secret, and _refuse_parser_mismatch refuses that URL before any request, the robots read's included (N1); the preflights call _guarded_redirect_get directly and get no typed read, the safe direction, and read kill_switch_active() (N2). Tests: tests/test_refusal_r620.py (80 cases: the real shape through a loopback proxy for four hosts with the R616 reader shown not to read it; EthicalFetcher.fetch against a user:pass@ URL directly and through the proxy, offline and credential-free; live proxies writing the guard's words as status line or 403 reason; eleven forged shapes from real exception objects; source pins on urllib3 and on the one writer; a walk of every exception class on the fetch path and its repr; 22 credential forms; both parsers reading the same host, port and path after the mask; ten non-credential @; five unreadable inputs; 4000 seeded fuzz inputs; DOTALL shown inert), tests/test_refusal_by_type_r620.py (16 cases: R619's shape through R619's real putrequest guard (skipped until #1855 lands), real requests and urllib3 and a loopback proxy, the fetcher answering the whole refusal sentence while the words read connect; the direct shape for http; no retry and no back-off after the typed refusal; an ordinary connection failure still a masked request error, retried; a fetch inside the except of a Stopped fetch and inside the except of a bare guard refusal, the switch clear, against a closed loopback port, still a request error and retried; a proxy answering the CONNECT with the guard's words as status line or 403 reason not offline; R619's shape built from the real classes, found through args and reason alone and through the fetcher; the refusal through __cause__ alone, and not through __context__ at the top or deeper; the depth bound and a loop; an exception that cannot be read as text, and a class only named AirplaneModeError), tests/test_failure_url_sites_r620.py (46 cases: nine sentences from the real EthicalFetcher against a 127.0.0.1 server, a 401, a 404, a PDF, a declared and a streamed oversize body, a slow body, a redirect loop, a robots.txt disallow and a robots.txt answering 500, each for a user:pass@ URL masked and an ordinary URL unchanged, and every reader shown to read the masked sentence as the raw one; a malformed URL and a redirect to ftp:// with credentials, inside their repr; the held-body size check through an injected session; the two log lines through caplog, their errors quoting the URL; requests' real InvalidURL quoting the credentialed URL, its userinfo taken out, and a three-character user withholding the error's words; userinfo_secrets' parts; the robots-cache and host-schedule DEBUG lines through caplog, masked, with an error that quotes the credentials; the pre-fetch guard is stubbed and OO_SSRF_CONNECT_GUARD=0 is set in the tests that reach the loopback server, which both guards refuse by design), tests/test_refusal_r620.py's fetcher case and tests/test_refusal_wrapped_shape.py's fetcher case now pin the whole refusal sentence (the live wrapped text still read as the switch's), tests/test_sink_sweep_records.py counts the walk's two uses of the caught exception as not a record (it reads no text, stores and logs nothing, like rollup_serve's chain walk), plus tests/test_kill_switch_refusal_constant.py, tests/test_csv_feeds_offline.py and tests/test_stop_is_not_an_outcome.py updated; green on urllib3 2.7.0 and 2.8.0. Sixteen mutants killed by named tests (alternative removed, four gaps, class name as \w+, mask removed, mask over the whole netloc, try/except removed, first @, dropped characters kept, authority ending at / only, leading whitespace kept, scheme prefix unchecked, DOTALL back, the base's behaviour); none survived. Thirteen more, one per wider-mask site with the raw URL put back, each killed by the site's credentialed test. Nine for the typed read, all killed: the walk removed, the walk stopping at the first level, the walk reading text, the walk reading the class name, a retry kept after the typed refusal, and each of the four links then followed dropped; the three links kept (__cause__, args, MaxRetryError.reason) were dropped again on the new walk, still killed. Thirteen for the folds, all killed: __context__ put back, __context__ followed unless suppressed (killed by the bare-refusal case alone, which is why both cases are there), no secrets at each of the five sites, the raw key in each of the two DEBUG lines, and the secrets as the whole userinfo only, with the @ kept, or without the dropped characters, and failure_netloc without its //. Not changed: the robots cache key and the host-schedule stamp keep scheme://netloc with its userinfo, so a credentialed host's user and password reach robots.json and host_schedule.json (the fix is the key itself, a behaviour change of the cache; the two persistence-failure DEBUG lines that name the key are now masked, Steward 3 #2, which leaves the files as where it is held); the robots.txt request carries the page URL's userinfo; activity_monitor.fetch_started keeps the raw URL and its netloc as the host; and the URL log lines in services/duckduckgo.py, utils/url_utils.py, utils/security.py and services/link_analyzer are outside the fetcher. Release-notes line: When collection is stopped while it runs through a local proxy such as Privoxy, the app now reports those sources as offline instead of as connection failures, and a web address that carries a user name and password no longer shows them in any fetch error message, whether the fetch met an HTTP error, a robots.txt refusal, a size or content-type limit or a redirect.
